language.script: Assamese-Bengali script (Assam); Latin script common in several hill states
language.sample_text: সাৱধান — বাটৰ নিৰ্মাণ কাম চলি আছে
language.script_notes: Assamese uses a script very close to Bengali; several of the hill states (Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya) use Latin-script local languages due to Christian missionary influence, unlike almost anywhere else in India — a strong regional tell.
false_friends: Myanmar/mainland Southeast Asia (shared hill/forest terrain and some ethnic ties)
Bangladesh (shared Bengali-adjacent script and Brahmaputra/Ganges delta geography)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: More essential given steep hill roads in the hill states.
road_furniture.curb_style: Generally less dense/chaotic traffic than the Gangetic Plain's major cities.

architecture.roof_style: Steeper pitched roofs more common than the flat-concrete national default, reflecting heavier rainfall; elevated stilt construction common in flood-prone Assam.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal roofing widespread, reflecting both rainfall and a lighter-construction tradition than the rest of India.
architecture.wall_construction: Bamboo and other light materials are far more common in traditional construction than the brick/concrete of the rest of India, given the region's earthquake and flood exposure; stilt houses common in Assam's flood-prone areas.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Natural bamboo/timber tones; church architecture (often white, simple, steepled) common in the Christian-majority hill states — a strong visual departure from Hindu-temple-dominant imagery elsewhere in India.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Stilt houses in flood-prone Assam; simple steepled Christian churches in Nagaland/Mizoram/Meghalaya (majority-Christian states, unusual within India); tea plantation architecture in Assam.

nature.vegetation: Lush, dense subtropical and montane forest across the hill states; the vast Brahmaputra river valley and its tea plantations in Assam; among the wettest regions on Earth (Meghalaya's Cherrapunji/Mawsynram).
nature.terrain: Rugged, forested hill country forms most of the region — the only part of India that geographically forms a land bridge to Southeast Asia; the wide, flood-prone Brahmaputra valley cuts through Assam.
nature.climate_signature: Consistently humid and green, among the highest rainfall in the world in parts of Meghalaya — a visually lush, misty, hilly look distinct from the rest of India.

vehicles.plate_color: Assam ('AS'), Nagaland ('NL'), Meghalaya ('ML') and other state codes distinct from the rest of India.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Generally lighter, less congested traffic than the major Gangetic Plain or South Indian cities.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Sparser than the rest of India, with real gaps in the more remote hill states.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Among the least-covered parts of India — genuine gaps across the hill states outside Guwahati and a handful of other towns.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared hilly forested terrain and some ethnic/cultural ties given the region's role as a land bridge
confusion_set.tiebreaker: India drives on the left as does Myanmar, but Indian plate formats, Latin-script Naga/Mizo/Khasi signage (rather than Burmese script) and continued use of Hindi/English alongside local languages separate Northeast India from Myanmar.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Bengali-adjacent script (Assamese is closely related to Bengali) and shared Brahmaputra/Ganges delta lowland geography
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bangladesh uses Bengali script specifically and drives on the left with its own distinct plate format; Assam's script differs subtly from Bengali, and India's national plate format (state code + RTO + series) differs from Bangladesh's.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national plate format
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Northeast India's Christian churches, bamboo/stilt construction and Latin-script hill-state languages are unlike anywhere else in Hindu-temple-dominant mainland India.
